svg.text: Title 12 is young, with an old tail that is mostly not law
Every in-force section of CFR Title 12 by the decade it was last amended. The deep tail looks alarming until you separate the genre sitting in it.
Of the 60 sections last touched before 1980, 46 (77%) are published interpretations — Board and agency rulings that are superseded by new ones, never edited in place.
Across the whole 30-years-and-older population the share is 39% (75 of 194). Ageing text is not the same as neglected rules.
The modern code dominates: 1,853 sections were amended in the 2010s or later.
The same tail, magnified about twenty times
Only the five oldest decades, rescaled so the bars are legible. Note how much of each is orange.
decade the section was last amended
A 1946 Board ruling on prompt settlement by broker-dealer customers. Interpretations are superseded, not amended — age is not decay here.
FDIC's five categories of bank business: commercial, trust, savings, industrial, cash depository. Operative, and simply never needed changing.
Farm Credit bond procedure, delegated to operating instructions in 1972 — the substance moved outside the CFR, so the section stopped ageing.
Source: eCFR full-text API, snapshot 2026-09-01. In-force sections carrying their own Federal Register source note. “Interpretation” is the publisher's own subject-group label.
